newsitem.title: TAIWAN: E.Asia Oilseeds- Taiwan frets over low bean stocks.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds- Taiwan frets over low bean stocks.

text.p: Taiwanese oilseed buyers greeted with gloom on Friday the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) monthly crop report released overnight, saying they may have to enter the market soon to buy up to 70,000 tonnes of soybeans.
"The overall soybean stocks are still relatively too low," Jack Lee, a soybean buyer at Taiwan's Hui Shung Agriculture and Food Corp, told Reuters by telephone.
The USDA estimated soybean ending stocks for the 1996/97 season at 130 million bushels on Thursday, up five million bushels from the previous report but down from last year's 183 million bushels.

Taiwanese dealers said they remained concerned about low world soybean stocks and that this may force them into the market earlier than they would want to despite the bearish reaction to the USDA report.

The Hui Shung Group may tender over the next two weeks for a shipment of 46,000 tonnes of soybeans and traders said Taiwanese buyers would need to secure a total of 70,000 tonnes of old crop soybeans soon.
Other East Asian oilseed buyers were less worried, with Japan hoping the bearish numbers will push prices down on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) while South Koreans ignored the report.
"We're going to be sidelined until the spot (CBOT soybean) contract falls at least below the US$7.50 (a bushel) level," an official at a major edible oil maker in Japan said.

The Japanese hopes may have been dashed after the CBOT's Project A after-hours trading system showed the July soybean contract up nine U.S. cents from the CBOT close at $8.50-1/2 a bushel at 0900 GMT.
Japan's Food Agency is more worried about the sharp fluctuations in the yen against the U.S. dollar rather than the Chicago market.
The agency, Japan's sole importer of wheat, barley and rice, was forced to postpone some grain import tenders on Thursday due to the yen's sharp slide against the dollar, traders said.
The dollar climbed above 115 yen on Thursday, compared with the Wednesday U.S. level of 111.29 to the dollar.
"(The) weak yen forced them to postpone some buying. They're increasingly worried about rising import costs," a wheat trader at a major trade house in Japan said.
South Korean oilseed buyers, however, ignored the USDA report, prefering to wait for the USDA's quarterly report at the end of the month.
"Normally we are not paying much attention to the June monthly report by the USDA," a trader said, adding the quarterly report is seen as more important than the monthly June crop report.

A group known as the Feed Buying Group invited tenders for 29,500 tonnes of rapeseed meal on Friday. It also invited bids for 8,600 tonnes of cottonseed meal, 8,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellet and 3,000 tonnes of wheat bran pellet, dealers said.
